text:
maya: Heads-up — I found a mismatch in the API reference for the uploads endpoint (/v1/uploads). The current docs PR shows the request as application/json with a base64 `file` field, but the hosted API (and our cURL examples) should use multipart/form-data. I hit a 415 when testing the docs snippet.
maya: Bad example from the PR:
```bash
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/uploads \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \
  -X POST \
  -d '{\"file\":\"<base64>\",\"filename\":\"pic.png\"}'
```
maya: That one fails for hosted. We should show a canonical multipart example and optionally a JSON/base64 variant with a clear note about hosted vs dedicated/private behavior.
ryan: I can update the OpenAPI requestBody to list both media types (multipart/form-data + application/json) and add code samples. Quick question: do we want to keep the base64 JSON sample in the main API ref or move it to an appendix/compatibility note?
leah: @sanjay any runtime constraints to call out? I remember some on-prem integrations only accept JSON payloads.
sanjay: Short answer: hosted API expects multipart/form-data for file uploads. Dedicated/private deployments may accept a JSON base64 payload if the customer enables the legacy-uploads flag (some older on-prem agents only handled JSON). So yes — canonical: multipart for hosted; show JSON as an alternate for dedicated/on-prem with a clear caveat.
maya: Proposed doc change (concise):
- Update OpenAPI to accept both media types (oneOf)
- Replace the broken cURL JSON example with a multipart cURL + python requests + node fetch
- Add a small section "Alternate payload: JSON (base64)" with note: \"Only supported on Dedicated/Private when legacy-uploads is enabled; not accepted by Hosted API.\"
maya: Example multipart cURL to include:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/uploads \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \
  -F \"file=@./pic.png\" \
  -F \"filename=pic.png\"
```
maya: Minimal python requests snippet for multipart:
```python
import requests
r = requests.post(
  \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/uploads\",
  headers={\"Authorization\": f\"Bearer {KEY}\"},
  files={\"file\": open(\"pic.png\", \"rb\")},
  data={\"filename\": \"pic.png\"}
)
print(r.status_code, r.json())
```
ryan: I'll open a small PR with OpenAPI + examples. I think we should show the JSON/base64 variant under a heading "Alternate: JSON/base64 (Dedicated only)" and keep the primary GET/POST examples multipart-first.
ryan: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/912 (WIP) — will add the snippets above and update the schema oneOf.
leah: Also update the SDK snippets section — the JS/Python SDK helpers currently accept a file path or bytes and will pick multipart automatically. We should show the convenience wrapper example so users don't end up hand-crafting fetch with form-data.
maya: Good call. Example SDK snippet (JS):
```js
import Redwood from '@redwoodai/sdk'
const client = new Redwood(process.env.KEY)
await client.uploadFile({ path: './pic.png', filename: 'pic.png' })
```
ryan: @sanjay can you double-check the wording about legacy flag and Dedicated behaviour? I don't want to accidentally claim hosted supports base64.
sanjay: LGTM — I'll leave a review on the PR to verify the wording.
_docs-preview-bot: Preview deployed for PR 912 — https://docs-preview.redwood.ai/pr/912/uploads-examples — please sanity-check the samples and callouts._
leah: Nice, I reviewed the preview. The multipart examples render fine. Two tiny nits: 1) call out the header `Content-Type: multipart/form-data` in the cURL example (curl auto adds it but mention it), 2) add a one-liner about max file size for hosted.
maya: Added to the PR notes — thanks. Assigning reviews: ryan -> author, sanjay -> technical review, leah -> docs review. Will merge after approvals.
ryan: Thanks — will ping when ready. :thumbsup:
